gui.intel_corrupted_msg:
Detected that your CPU is affected by a critical Intel chip bug.

If you are not familiar with this issue, it is highly recommended to read this $LINK.INTEL_CHIP_BUG_FAQ$. DO NOT report this crash until you have:
  • Updated your BIOS.
  • Made sure that the crash is not caused by this bug, as the issue won't be resolved even after a BIOS update if the CPU has already started dying. It is important to note that this update will not fix damaged hardware. If the PC has crashed or been unstable due to this issue, the CPU is damaged.
  • If the CPU is damaged, replace it under warranty. Intel has extended the warranty for affected processors by two years.
This warning doesn't indicate that this crash is 100% caused by this issue, but before reporting, you must check that a corrupted CPU is not the reason.
gui.duplicated_mod_warn:
If you are seeing this message while trying to run the modpack,it means the modpack
installation is corrupted (possibly due to an incorrect update). To fix this, you need to reinstall the modpack.

Detected multiple mods with mod_id "crash_assistant", leave only one of them:
warnings.atio6axx: The atio6axx "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file, is part of the AMD driver for the GPU, there's a bad version of the AMD drivers that instantly crashes on an OpenGL task. Reinstall/Fresh install your drivers from $LINK.AMD_SUPPORT$ IF you do not have an AMD GPU, then you need to set your system to be using that GPU instead of the AMD integrated GPU on the CPU, steps below. $LINK.HOW_FORCE_APP_USE_DISCRETE_GPU$
warnings.nvoglv64: The nvoglv64 "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file, is part of the Nvidia driver for the GPU. This can be an issue with your current Nvidia card driver. Reinstall/Fresh install your drivers from $LINK.NVIDIA_DRIVERS$
warnings.jemalloc: The jemalloc "Problematic frame" in $LOG_FILENAME$ indicates an issue with the jemalloc memory allocator. To resolve this, add the following argument to your JVM args: -Dorg.lwjgl.system.allocator=system
warnings.jvm: The jvm.dll "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file may result from various issues, including a hardware bug or a bug in the JVM itself. Please try the following steps in order: 1) Have you seen our warning about Intel 13th and 14th‑generation processors? If you’ve experienced any system instability (BSODs, random app crashes), this is likely the cause. 2) If memory overclocking (XMP/DOCP/EXPO) is enabled, disable it, as it doesn’t seem to work well with your system and may be causing memory corruption. Look for memeory diagnostics instructions in the buttom of this message. 3) Apply the recommended JVM arguments for your modpack. 4) Test different Java versions or vendors, as the bug may come from the current JVM installation version or vendor. 5) Try reducing active CPU count like this, via JVM argument: -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=$HALF_OF_PROCESSORS$ 6) If none of the above helps, contact support. Memory diagnostics instructions: 1) Save this $LINK.RESULTS_OF_MEMORY_DIAGNOSTICS$. It will be needed to get results of diagnostics after reboot. 2) Press win + R to open the Run dialog box, enter mdsched and click OK. 3) In the Windows Memory Diagnostic window, click the Restart now and check for problems option. If you don’t see a popup with the results after reboot, refer to the instructions on how to view them. Please note: this test may not detect every memory issue, and it won’t confirm if the JVM crash is 100% caused by memory. Disabling memory overclocking is still the best first step.
warnings.libglfw_so: The libglfw.so "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file is a typical Linux problem. To fix it, follow the steps below: 1. Download the latest GLFW library files from your distro's official repositories. If you are on a slow updating distro (like Ubuntu), instead download the latest pre-built files from this $LINK.GLFW_DOWNLOAD$ 2. Add -Dorg.lwjgl.glfw.libname=/path/to/file to your launcher java arguments. An example of what this might look like is -Dorg.lwjgl.glfw.libname=/home/frontear/Downloads/libglfw.so. $LANG.warnings_common.so_vm_options$
warnings.libopenal_so: The libopenal.so "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file is a typical Linux problem. To fix it, follow the steps below: 1. Download the latest OpenAL library files from your distro's official repositories. 2. Add -Dorg.lwjgl.openal.libname=/usr/lib/libopenal.so to your launcher java arguments. This path might differ depending on your distribution, so please double-check. $LANG.warnings_common.so_vm_options$
warnings.macjdk: The v ~StubRoutines::SafeFetch32 "Problematic Frame" error in $LOG_FILENAME$ is caused by an issue with the bundled Java runtime ("Microsoft" build version 17.0.8 and newer) on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/etc.) CPUs, which causes Java to crash under certain conditions. To resolve this issue, you first need to install a different Java runtime: 1. Click $LINK.AZUL_DOWNLOAD$ to get the recommended Java version for your system. 2. Hover the Download button and click ".dmg" to download the installer. 3. Open the downloaded file and follow the installation instructions. Next, you need to configure your Minecraft launcher to use the newly installed Java. The following instructions are for $LINK.ATL$ and may vary for other launchers: 1. Click "Settings" on the right. 2. Select "Java/Minecraft" at the top. 3. Uncheck "Use Java Provided by Minecraft". 4. Manually enter the following Java path in the "Java Install Location" text box: /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/zulu-21.jdk/Contents/Home/bin/java
warnings.lib_gl_programmability: The libGLProgrammability.dylib “Problematic frame” in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file is caused by a bug in Apple’s in‑house OpenGL driver, this blocks many advanced shader packs from working on macOS. Apple makes all the drivers in‑house; fixes only arrive via macOS updates. Most likely you are using an incompatible shader pack with macOS. Disable shaders or switch to a shader pack compatible with macOS. Note: This has been an issue since 2021, so it’s most likely still not fixed.
warnings.insufficient_memory: The There is insufficient memory... message in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: Your system is running out of available physical RAM or swap space. To fix this, make sure your memory isn't heavily used by other running applications — check using Task Manager, and try to keep unnecessary programs closed while playing Minecraft. Ensure you are using the recommended memory settings for this modpack — perhaps your Xmx value is set too high? If you followed some dumb internet advices about disabling page files, revert it — that's likely the cause. Check your disk space. If you're running out of it, there might not be enough space for the swap area, so you'll need to free up some space to fix the issue. Sometimes, simply restarting your computer can help clear out memory and reset swap usage. If you're using more than the recommended memory settings for this pack, try lowering them. If none of this helps
warnings.insufficient_memory_indv: try the following: * Installing the $LINK.FERRITE_CORE$ mod * Installing the $LINK.MODERN_FIX$ mod with dynamic_resources and deduplicate_location enabled. * Removing some mods to reduce Minecraft's RAM usage
warnings.out_of_memory_error: The java.lang.OutOfMemoryError message in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: There isn't enough memory allocated for Minecraft to continue running. Look up the recommended memory settings for this modpack and allocate more memory. If you're sure you've allocated enough RAM
warnings.disk_space_ended: The message java.io.IOException: There is not enough space on the disk in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: There wasn't enough space on the disk to complete an operation. You are running out of disk space! Clear some space to resolve the issue.
warnings.closed_by_windows: If this crash happened during game or level loading, it was likely caused by pressing keys or clicking the mouse. The error "The program javaw.exe version ... stopped interacting with Windows and was closed" in $LOG_FILENAME$ means the game froze, possibly due to these actions. To avoid this, let the game load fully—DO NOT CLICK ANYTHING, PRESS ANY KEY, or CLICK END PROCESS. If the crash occurred during mid-gameplay, just press OK and ignore this message.
warnings.curseforge_corrupted: We detected signs in the $LOG_FILENAME$ that your Minecraft installation is corrupted by CurseForge. To fix it, follow the steps below: 1. Open your modpack folder in File Explorer. 2. Go up two levels. 3. Nuke the Install folder. Another solution is switching to another launcher that doesn't have such problems, like $LINK.ATL$.
warnings.resource_location_exception: We detected signs in $LOG_FILENAME$ that your game encountered a resource location error: $LINE_FROM_LOG$. This typically happens when Minecraft tries to load a resource (such as a block, item, or texture) using a name that contains invalid characters. This is most often caused by one of the following reasons: 1) Non-English system language settings. In such cases, the resource location may include a Unicode symbol in this format: \u0131n. To fix this, add the following JVM arguments to force the game to use English locale settings: -Duser.language=en -Duser.region=US 2) A mod has incorrectly handled a resource location. Try removing the mod that added this faulty resource. It is strongly recommended to try the first solution before resorting to the second one.
warnings.c6a: We detected signs in $LOG_FILENAME$ of missing Create mod classes, while the Create mod is currently installed. Create Update 6 was released recently, and you may have one of the following mismatches: - Create Update 5 with addons for Update 6, or - Create Update 6 with addons for Update 5. (Addons here refer to any mod that integrates with Create, including both standard addons and mods with Create compatibility.) You'll need to ensure that all Create-related mods are either from Update 5 or Update 6. Note that release dates are not a fully reliable way to determine compatibility. This may be a false alarm, so please double-check. To identify which mods are incompatible with your current version of the Create mod: Click OK, then open on top of the window $LANG.gui.menu.analysis$ -> $LANG.gui.menu.analysis.create_dependencies$. Wait for the process to finish—you'll then see a list of mods that are incompatible with the installed version of Create.
warnings.ctov_without_lithostitched:
Detected that you are using the CTOV (ChoiceTheorem's Overhauled Village) mod without $LINK.LITHOSTITCHED$.
Technically, CTOV will work on its own, but as soon as other mods are involved, it stops working.
If your modpack includes many mods, this is most likely the issue, and installing $LINK.LITHOSTITCHED$ should fix it.
warnings.duplicated_mods: At the end of $LOG_FILENAME$, we found an error about duplicated mods: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ To fix this crash, keep only one of the mods listed above.
warnings.modernifx_watchdog: At the end of $LOG_FILENAME$, we found a message from the IntegratedWatchdog about one server tick took way longer than it should have: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ If you weren’t doing something extremely slow, like using WorldEdit to change trillions of blocks, this likely means the Integrated Server has deadlocked. A deadlock happens when parts of the game are waiting on each other in a way that prevents anything from continuing — like a traffic jam where every car is blocking another. To fix this crash, check the thread dump at the end of the log. It shows which parts of the game were waiting on each other. This can be hard to understand without technical knowledge. You can try using some advanced reasoning AI tool to analyze the thread dump — it may help identify the mod causing the issue. If this happened in an unmodified modpack, please report it to the developers — it shouldn’t happen.
warnings.optifine: Once upon a time, OptiFine was the go-to solution to make your game better, faster, and stronger through various useful features and optimizations. But things have changed. Currently, OptiFine is incompatible with A LOT of mods, and this crash was most likely caused by one of these issues. There is no longer a good reason to use it. Other open-source projects offer better performance, significantly improved compatibility, and full shader support. Read this article and consider switching to an alternatives: $LINK.OPTIFINE_ALTERNATIVES$ If you are playing a modpack, it's most likely already well-optimized — you just need to remove OptiFine.
warnings.kubejs_datapack: We detected a KubeJS error in $LOG_FILENAME$: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ If this happened with an unmodified modpack, it most likely means your installation is corrupted. Please reinstall the modpack. If you are creating a modpack, the issue is most likely caused by a datapack applied through KubeJS. Read the error message carefully to fix the issue.
warnings.missing_unsupported_dependencie: We detected a dependency conflict in $LOG_FILENAME$: $LINE_FROM_LOG$ To fix this issue, read the message above carefully and try to resolve all conflicts. Involved mod IDs to JAR names map (for reference only): $MODIDS_TO_JARNAMES$
warnings.missing_embeddium_for_oculus: We detected signs in the $LOG_FILENAME$ that you are missing $LINK.EMBEDDIUM$ for Oculus. Installing $LINK.EMBEDDIUM$ mod will fix your issue.
warnings.rubidium:
Rubidium is an abandoned mod with numerous bugs and stability issues.
There’s no reason to use it—please switch to $LINK.EMBEDDIUM$ instead,
which is a fork that continues its development and is actively maintained.
There is a high likelihood that Rubidium specifically caused this crash.
warnings.integrated_gpu:

gui.privacy.title: Privacy Information
gui.privacy.mclogs_privacy_info:
Privacy:

Logs are uploaded only when the user explicitly chooses to do so and are sent to mclo.gs, a log-sharing service created by Aternos. Before a log is published, mclo.gs automatically redacts sensitive information—such as access tokens, IP addresses, usernames and etc—so it's safe to share. See their $LINK.MCLOGS_PRIVACY_POLICY$ for details.$GNOMEBOT_PRIVACY_INFO$ Until you share the link, no one except you and the mclo.gs administrators can access your logs.
gui.privacy.gnomebot_privacy_info: Because the mobile interface of mclo.gs is inconvenient, the generated link is—by default—wrapped through gnomebot.dev. For example: https://mclo.gs/X → https://gnomebot.dev/paste/mclogs/X This behavior is configurable. gnomebot.dev, created by LatvianModder—the developer behind the KubeJS mod and several FTB modpacks—is an open-source log viewer that fetches the log, applies cleaner formatting for readability, and does not store its content beyond a brief 5-minute cache.
gui.privacy.logs_upload_question: Do you accept the $LINK.PRIVACY_POLICY$ of uploading logs?
gui.privacy.declined: Failed to upload log because you declined the privacy policy, try again.
